entries.title: I Samuel 31:2
segments: Good men are, in the natural order of things, more or less involved in the calamities which wicked rulers bring upon themselves, and the state intrusted to their care.

entries.title: I Samuel 31:4
segments: The wicked are more afraid of men than they are of God, and seek the praise of men more than the praise of God.

entries.title: I Samuel 31:6
segments: Though the righteous and the wicked may here live and die together, yet in eternity they will be separated and be in states as diverse as heaven is from hell.

entries.title: I Samuel 31:9
segments: It matters little where the body is, or how it is treated after death, if the soul is freed from sin and happy with God in heaven; for the body in that case will soon rise in the likeness of Christ's glorified body, and with the soul shine for ever like the sun in the kingdom of God.

entries.title: I Samuel 31:10
segments:
Beth-shan; on the west of Jordan, and north-east of mount Gilboa. 
 
The final reward of resorting to unlawful means for deliverance from trouble and the maintenance of earthly power and honor, will be shame and ruin.

entries.title: I Samuel 31:11
segments: Jabesh-Gilead; in the tribe of Manasseh, east of Jordan.

entries.title: I Samuel 31:12
segments: The character of truly noble men appears most clearly in times of deep distress.
